intro: Imagine the end of a long day on the road, and gates opening to welcome you. This is Sultan Han Caravanserai, in Aksaray province, built in 1229: the largest Seljuk caravanserai in Anatolia. Here caravans on the Konya–Aksaray road were housed and fed, and their animals shod, for three days at no charge.
history: Sultan Han was built in 1229 for Alâeddin Keykubad I, and it was the largest stop for caravans on the Konya–Aksaray–Kayseri road. After a fire it was enlarged at the end of the thirteenth century to more than four thousand square metres. Notice its two halves: an open summer court paired with a covered winter hall. That pairing is the standard Seljuk plan.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal, then step into the courtyard with its kiosk mosque, and continue to the covered winter hall and the stables and stores.
facts: Did you know? In a Seljuk han, lodging, food and the shoeing of animals were free for three days, paid for by the endowment that ran the building. The kiosk mosque in the middle of the court stands on four piers, so a loaded caravan could pass right beneath it into the yard. And the han is split between an open summer court and a covered winter hall — the Anatolian winter, in a sense, wrote the Seljuk plan.
outro: This brings our journey through Sultan Han Caravanserai to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Travellers have rested within these walls for centuries; may your own road ahead be a good one. Enjoy your visit.
